## Overview

J-ROCKET AF randomized 1,280 Japanese patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation at increased risk for stroke to [rivaroxaban](./rivaroxaban.md) 15 mg once daily or to [warfarin](./warfarin.md) dose-adjusted according to Japanese guidelines. Its primary objective was to determine non-inferiority of rivaroxaban against warfarin for the principal safety outcome of major and non-major clinically relevant bleeding in the on-treatment safety population; the primary efficacy endpoint was the composite of stroke and systemic embolism ([src_81808a7c4c3bf0e34bac1c720768f46d](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_81808a7c4c3bf0e34bac1c720768f46d.md)).

## Reported results

Non-inferiority was confirmed: the principal safety outcome occurred at 18.04% per year with rivaroxaban and 16.42% per year with warfarin (hazard ratio 1.11; 95% CI 0.87 to 1.42; P<0.001 for non-inferiority). Intracranial hemorrhage rates were 0.8% with rivaroxaban and 1.6% with warfarin, with a strong trend toward reduced stroke or systemic embolism with rivaroxaban (hazard ratio 0.49; P=0.050) ([src_81808a7c4c3bf0e34bac1c720768f46d](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_81808a7c4c3bf0e34bac1c720768f46d.md)).

The trial is presented as a Japan-specific companion to the global ROCKET AF study, supporting the bridging of global ROCKET AF results into Japanese clinical practice ([src_81808a7c4c3bf0e34bac1c720768f46d](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_81808a7c4c3bf0e34bac1c720768f46d.md)).
